title: Take a new use case to proof
trigger: The Owner decides the product must let an actor do something new.
result: Every test of the use case passes and coverage shows it proved.
notes: LA-BO09 times this journey. The work passes from the Owner, who writes the use case, to an Agent, who builds and proves it. The Owner hands it over by asking Claude in the chat, with the use case in focus (LA-PLT-UC19): by the use-case line (LA-STD-MODELING-R15) that is the chat's goal with another message, not a goal of its own, and records carry no status that would mark a use case ready to build.

title: Bring a product onto Lathe
trigger: A team decides to specify its product with Lathe.
result: The product checks clean, with its business outcomes and domains written.
notes: LA-BO05 counts the products that adopt Lathe; this journey is how each one does, untimed.

title: Move a product to a new Lathe
result: The product checks clean on the new Lathe.
notes: The path to-dos left follows the move when it lists work to do by hand, in place of the main path's check.

title: Have Claude change the spec and accept it
trigger: The Owner asks Claude for a change in the desktop chat.
notes: LA-BO06 counts changes sent back for rework, from the merges the Owner reviews. On the path sent back, the Owner undoes the turn (LA-PLT-UC27), then tells Claude why in the chat (LA-PLT-UC19): by the use-case line (LA-STD-MODELING-R15) a send-back is the chat's goal with another message, not a goal of its own. The path sent back takes the place of the main path's last step, then goes back to its second.
